newsitem.title: CANADA: Police raid violent Quebec motorcycle gang.
newsitem.headline: Police raid violent Quebec motorcycle gang.

text.p: Police conducted a series of raids on Wednesday against a violent motorcycle gang involved in a bloody turf war with rivals that has killed 36 people in Quebec over the past three years.

In an unprecedented offensive across the French-speaking province of 7.1 million people, the provincial Surete du Quebec, municipal police forces and Royal Canadian Mounted Police (RCMP) arrested 20 alleged members of the Rock Machine motorcyle gang.
The Rock Machine has battled the rival Hell's Angels gang for control of Quebec's lucrative trade in illegal drugs and contraband alcohol and cigarettes.

Several alleged gang members were taken into custody at the group's fortified clubhouse in Beauport, just outside Quebec City, which police seized. Others were arrested in Montreal and smaller municipalities. In all, police acted on 70 search warrants.
The police also froze financial transactions in connection with the bikers' real estate properties and stores.
"In the province, 600 policemen are involved in 28 cities," Surete du Quebec spokesman Real Ouellet told Reuters.

The joint-forces "Wolverine" police squad planned to interview hundreds of people to obtain more information about the financial, real estate and alleged criminal operations of the Rock Machine, police said.

Flanked by Canadian Prime Minister Jean Chretien and Justice Minister Allan Rock at a news conference in Montreal, Montreal Urban Community Police Chief Jacques Duchesneau said a federal "anti-gang law" enacted last month made the raids possible.
"We got a new law that allowed us to carry out these operations," Duchesneau said.
Chretien was in Montreal campaigning for the June 2 national election.

The law gave police widers powers to investigate and prosecute gangs believed to be involved in criminal activity. It also allows police to seize assets involved in the commission of crimes by criminal gangs.

Since the battle between the Hell's Angels and Rock Machine biker groups erupted in mid-1994, 36 people have been killed in armed attacks and bombings of restaurants, bars and biker clubhouses in Quebec.
Almost all victims were gang members or suspected of being affiliated with them. But the car-bomb death in 1995 of an 11-year-old boy in Montreal galvanised public outrage against the bikers.
